definition: Semantic Scholar is a research tool for scientific literature.
details: It is developed at the Allen Institute for AI and was publicly released in November 2015. Semantic Scholar uses modern techniques in natural language processing to support the research process, for example by providing automatically generated summaries of scholarly papers. The Semantic Scholar team is actively researching the use of artificial intelligence in natural language processing, machine learning, human–computer interaction, and information retrieval. Semantic Scholar began as a database for the topics of computer science, geoscience, and neuroscience. In 2017, the system began including biomedical literature in its corpus. As of September 2022, it includes over 200 million publications from all fields of science.

explainer.lead: Semantic Scholar is a research tool for scientific literature built at the Allen Institute for AI and released publicly in November 2015. It matters because it applies NLP to help researchers find and digest papers.

tiers.eli5: It's a search engine for academic papers that can summarize them for you.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use it to search literature and get automatically generated summaries of papers; the team actively studies NLP, machine learning, human-computer interaction and information retrieval, so features evolve.
tiers.paperLevel: A research tool for scientific literature that uses modern NLP techniques, such as automatically generated paper summaries, to support the research process. It began as a database; its automated summaries are derived from paper text and inherit its limitations.

explainer.example: A researcher searching for a topic receives a list of papers plus short automatically generated summaries of each.
